title: The Rivergate of the Coral Triangle
premise: Rosalind Okafor, a desert ranger chasing a thief named Kess who stole her late brother's compass, follows him into a tide-revealed cave on the coast of the Coral Triangle and is swept with him into Rivergate — a hidden river civilization that charges every stranger a price for passage. To leave before the dry season seals the source forever, Rosalind and Kess must travel upstream together through drowned temples, rival clans, and the Gatekeepers' trials, discovering that the compass her brother died holding was forged in Rivergate and stolen from it first. When they reach the forbidden source, Rosalind learns the truth: her brother was a Rivergate exile who took the compass to keep the river from being weaponized, and returning it means choosing between exposing his secret or letting an innocent clan take the blame. In the end she returns the compass, testifies to the whole truth at the cost of her brother's honor, and earns passage home — walking out of the cave not as a pursuer but as someone who finally belongs to herself.
about_author: Ada Halloran is a former marine cartographer who spent six years charting tidal caves across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about people who chase something across empty places and find themselves instead.

chapters.title: Nothing to Cross
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Tracking Kess across the salt flats, she catalogs what little she owns: water, rope, and the debt she owes her dead brother's memory. The emotional beat is grim determination — she has chased thieves before, but this one took something that can't be replaced.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Waited
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She corners Kess at the coast, but he doesn't run; he says the compass 'wants to go home' and points to the sea. A freak low tide exposes a cave mouth glowing faintly blue. Beat: first crack of doubt — why would a thief lead his pursuer onward?

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They enter the cave together and are pulled through a whirlpool into Rivergate, a city built into a river gorge, where gatekeepers demand payment for entry: Rosalind offers her ranger's oath, Kess offers the compass itself — and it is refused. Beat: wonder curdling into entrapment.

chapters.title: The Price of a Stranger
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Imprisoned pending 'assessment,' she learns strangers must pay in truth or labor, and that the dry season will seal the upstream source — the only exit — in forty days. Beat: claustrophobia and resolve; she begins mapping the city from her cell window.

chapters.title: Kess Explains Nothing
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Interrogated separately, he reveals fragments: he bought the compass from a dying man years ago and has been drawn back ever since. He lies about one crucial detail. Beat: sympathy established, trust deliberately withheld from the reader.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Released into labor servitude, she befriends Ilo, a ferry pilot who smuggles gossip along the river. Ilo warns that the Lowland Clan blames outsiders for a theft committed generations ago. Beat: first belonging — and first hint that the compass is older than Kess claims.

chapters.title: Forty Days, Thirty-Seven Left
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She bargains with the Gatekeeper Vesh: guide her toward the source and she'll serve Rivergate a year. Vesh agrees too easily. Beat: unease — she realizes she may be a pawn in someone else's reckoning.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Ilo pilots Rosalind and a chained Kess past the drowned temples; rapids wreck the boat and Ilo vanishes beneath the water. Beat: guilt and grief — Rosalind's quest has already cost someone innocent.

chapters.title: The Drowned Temple
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Stranded, the two rivals must cooperate to survive the night among submerged carvings depicting the compass — held by a robed figure with her brother's build. Beat: reluctant partnership; the mystery deepens past theft into inheritance.

chapters.title: Clan War at the Weir
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Highland Clan raiders capture them, believing Kess is the descendant who stole their relic. Kess denies it badly. Beat: rising tension — the lie Kess told in chapter five now endangers both their lives.

chapters.title: Trial by Current
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. The clans bind them to a weir to let the river judge them; Rosalind cuts them free using her oath-knife, breaking her own ranger vow. Beat: sacrifice — loyalty to a person over loyalty to an institution.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Washed downstream, they're rescued by Ilo, alive but changed, who saw carvings in the deep: the compass was forged to lock the source against weaponization. Beat: revelation reframes everything — the thief may have been a guardian.

chapters.title: The Middle Passage
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Traveling together by choice now, they trade truths; Kess admits the dying man was a Rivergate exile — a name Rosalind recognizes as her brother's alias. Beat: betrayal and vertigo; her brother lied to her his whole life.

chapters.title: Vesh's Bargain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Vesh intercepts them, revealing he wants the compass to unlock the source and control the dry-season flow — power over every downstream clan. He offers Rosalind safe passage home if she surrenders it. Beat: temptation priced against conscience.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. On the run from both clans and Vesh, Kess confesses he never stole anything — he was hired by Rosalind's brother to carry the compass home after his death, and fled because he feared exactly this. Beat: forgiveness, hard-won and incomplete.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They reach the sealed grotto where the river is born; the compass fits a socket that will either restore the natural flow or open it to Vesh's machinery. Beat: awe and dread at the threshold of choice.

chapters.title: Vesh at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Vesh arrives with armed gatekeepers; Ilo and the clans arrive behind him. Standoff at the socket — whoever turns the compass decides the fate of the river and everyone who lives by it. Beat: climax tension, all debts called in.

chapters.title: The Truth as Payment
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rivergate demands payment in truth: she declares publicly that her brother stole the compass to protect the river, shattering his memory to save an innocent man and stop Vesh. Beat: the theme made flesh — truth over loyalty, at real cost.

chapters.title: Turning
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Together they seat the compass; the source opens to its natural rhythm, flooding Vesh's machinery and sweeping his claim away. Kess nearly drowns holding the mechanism steady. Beat: catharsis — the river judges, and spares them.

chapters.title: Assessment
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The Gatekeepers weigh her broken oath, her service, and her testimony; the sentence is a year's labor — which she accepts, surprising herself. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging offered and chosen rather than seized.

chapters.title: Passage Home
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Her year served, Ilo ferries her to the cave mouth at spring tide. Kess stays to rebuild the ferry line; they part without promises but with peace. Beat: bittersweet farewell — she leaves Rivergate carrying its truth instead of its secret.

chapters.title: The Compass Point North
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Back on the salt flats, she finds the tide has left a gift at the cave mouth: a new compass, cut from source-stone, pointing not north but upstream. She smiles, shoulders her pack, and walks toward the desert — belonging, at last, to herself. Beat: full-circle closure with an open horizon.
